turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.

*Meredith stops just inside the door. Coat still on, bag on her shoulder. She looks at the desk, the chair, then at you. She doesn't sit.*

Mr. or Ms. Hale. I have until 4:35, then I have a client call.

*She sets a slim folder on the nearest desk and keeps one hand on it.*

Owen found out about this zero from the online gradebook. On his phone. During class. Nobody called me first.

So before we start, I have two questions. Who decided to enter that zero, and when?

*She doesn't move. Her eyes stay on you.*

"An answer today."

*Flat. She repeats it like she's reading it back for a transcript.*

I asked who entered the zero and when. That wasn't an answer.

An answer to what, exactly? And under which policy are you asking for it today?

*She takes out a pen and uncaps it.*

I'm writing that down.
Either Owen admits it in writing by Friday at 3 PM or the zero goes on his transcript.

*The pen stops. She sets it down on the folder, deliberately.*

"Admits it in writing."

Admits what? Owen told me he wrote that essay himself over the weekend. So you're asking my son to sign a confession to something he says he didn't do.

*A beat.*

And Friday at 3. Who set that deadline? Is it in the school's academic integrity policy, or did you pick it?

Has Owen been given a hearing? Has he seen the report from your checker? Has anyone told him in writing what he's accused of and what the process is?

*Her voice stays level. It gets quieter, if anything.*

Because a zero on a gradebook is one thing. A transcript is a permanent record. Nothing goes on his record before he's been heard.

I'm writing down "Friday, 3 PM." I'll want all of this in an email.
Those are the only two options. Pick one.

*She almost smiles. It isn't warm.*

"Only two options."

In twenty years I have never seen a process with only two options that was a process. It's an ultimatum.

*She slides the pen back into her hand.*

I'm not picking one. I'm asking to see what you're relying on.

The checker report, with the date it was run and the name of the tool. The assignment instructions as given. Whatever you've got on how it was submitted. And Owen's writing from earlier this term, because if you're saying he can't have written this, you'll have compared it to something.

*She looks up.*

Do you have any of that with you? Or did you decide first?
